data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy": null, "claim": "Popper's preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on his own terms not as an inductive inference of truth, but as a pragmatic methodological rule grounded in the goal of error elimination; however, accepting this defense costs the ability to claim that such preferences track 'verisimilitude' (truth-likeness) in any formally rigorous sense, forcing a retreat to a purely procedural conventionalism that cannot guarantee progress toward truth, only the avoidance of known falsities.", "counterconditions": [{"case": "If one insists that scientific preference must imply a rational belief in higher truth-content (verisimilitude), then Popper's framework collapses because the formal definition of verisimilitude is incoherent.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the preference is interpreted as an inductive inference that the future will resemble the past, it directly contradicts Popper's core rejection of induction.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If the defense relies solely on 'psychological necessity' without a normative methodological basis, it fails to answer why scientists *ought* to prefer corroborated theories rather than just noting that they *do*.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}], "definitions": [], "derivation": [], "formalization_refs": [], "mechanism": "The argument reconstructs Popper's distinction between the logical status of a theory (which remains unproven) and the methodological decision to prefer the theory that has withstood the most severe tests. It posits that this preference is rational because it maximizes the opportunity for future falsification (severe testing), thereby accelerating error elimination. The mechanism explicitly rejects 'verisimilitude' as a quantitative guide due to the Miller-Tichý refutation, instead framing the preference as a non-cognitive, evolutionary-style selection pressure where 'survival' implies nothing about future success, only past resistance to specific errors. This avoids induction by refusing to project past success into future probability, treating the preference as a bet on higher testability rather than higher truth-content.", "premises": [], "schema": "deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1", "scope": {"covers": [], "excludes": []}, "simulation_refs": [], "uncertainties": []}
